acceptance: Every shard artifact from a real canary run contains a JUnit XML file with per-test durations.
Setup time and test time per shard are recoverable from the run (step timings or a small summary field).
Workflow contract tests assert the JUnit output path and that the marker expression, shard count, and aggregation are unchanged.
context:
PR #2340 open against develop: branch fix/canary-junit-durations, commit 4067f2dce (rebased onto 90a76a336). make pr-preflight green at that head: focused fast lane 2120 passed / 21 skipped, medium-tier exit 0, required-pr-preflight exit 0, ordered_success; receipts reused on re-check. Workflow contract tests assert the JUnit path and that marker expression, shard count, and aggregation are unchanged. Both shard branches simulated locally (empty shard -> fallback report marked junit_captured=false; populated shard -> real JUnit), and the summary JSON parses with the marker expression intact. release_canary_incident.py only globs shard-*-pytest.log, so the new XML files do not affect the incident job.

Note for whoever runs preflight here: BENCHBOX_TEST_LOCK_WAIT_SECONDS matches VALIDATION_ENV_PREFIXES (BENCHBOX_), so changing its value between runs forks the receipt identity and forces full re-execution. Keep one value per branch. Under heavy local load, tests/integration/test_database_integration.py::test_database_resource_management (RSS growth < 50MB) can fail on macOS; CI runs make test-medium on ubuntu-latest only, and it fails in isolation on unrelated trees, so it is a pre-existing environment flake, not a regression from this branch.

Remaining acceptance item: verify JUnit XML and setup/test timings appear in a real canary run's shard artifacts. That needs a live release-canary run after merge.

description:
The pre-merge canary-impact selector needs measured per-test durations to size shards and to estimate runner-minutes and wall time; selected-file counts alone cannot establish cost, because each shard also pays several minutes of setup and test runtimes vary widely. Today the canary shards write only a pytest text log.

Change: each release-canary.yml shard also writes a JUnit XML report (pytest --junitxml) into its existing uploaded artifact directory, and the run records per-shard setup time (checkout, uv sync) separately from test time.
